title: What offline reason does Jenkins display?
summary: Triage manual and monitor-driven offline states before changing launch, network, runtime, or credentials.

choices.label: A node monitor took the agent offline
Offline reason is unavailable or unclear

title: Was the offline state intentional?
summary: A user with the required Jenkins permission may deliberately mark an agent temporarily offline. Confirm intent before reconnecting it.

choices.label: Yes, maintenance or another approved reason is active
No, the authorized owner confirms it should return

title: Keep the intentional offline boundary in place
summary: Do not override a deliberate maintenance or safety decision. Confirm the planned return condition with the owner.

choices.label: Authorized owner confirms the agent can return
Maintenance or safety condition remains active

title: Return the agent only with authorized confirmation
summary: Use Jenkins to remove the temporary-offline state only after the owner confirms maintenance, capacity, and workload-safety conditions are satisfied.
prerequisites: Agent owner or authorized operator confirmed
rollback: Mark the agent temporarily offline again if validation fails or the maintenance condition returns.
verification: Agent is online for the intended reason and accepts only appropriate workloads.

title: Which monitor took the agent offline?
summary: Inspect the exact monitor and underlying condition. Do not disable monitors to make the status disappear.

title: Resolve the measured storage condition
summary: Inspect the affected filesystem or temporary directory, ownership, and growth source. Keep the monitor enabled while correcting the underlying condition.

choices.label: Storage ownership or cleanup safety is unclear

title: Correct clock synchronization evidence
summary: Confirm controller and agent time sources, drift, and synchronization health before reconnecting the agent.

title: Resolve the measured resource pressure
summary: Inspect memory, swap, and workload pressure. Do not disable the monitor or run the agent as root to bypass the condition.

choices.label: Capacity or workload ownership is unclear

title: Inspect the exact health or plugin monitor
summary: Use the monitor message and plugin documentation to verify the measured condition. Do not disable the monitor as a routine fix.

title: Verify the monitor clears for the right reason
summary: Confirm the measured value is healthy and Jenkins no longer keeps the agent offline. If manual intervention is required, use an authorized path.
verification: The exact monitor reports a healthy value
The agent is no longer held offline by that monitor
The condition does not immediately recur

title: How is the agent launched?
summary: For genuine connection or launch failures, the safest evidence depends on whether the controller connects outward or the agent connects inward.

title: What does the Jenkins agent log report?
summary: Inspect the controller-side launch log before changing credentials or networking.

title: Can the agent reach the controller endpoint?
summary: Inbound agents depend on controller URL, secret, Java/Remoting compatibility, and network policy.

choices.label: DNS, TLS, proxy, or connection failure

title: Is the agent process or service running?
summary: A stopped local process should be diagnosed in its own execution context.

choices.label: Process runs but Jenkins shows offline

title: What happened to the container or Pod?
summary: Ephemeral agents may terminate, remain Pending, or fail before connecting.

title: Resolve the controller or agent hostname in the real execution context
summary: Do not substitute a public resolver or hosts entry before identifying the DNS layer.

title: Inspect the exact controller-agent network path
summary: Confirm source, destination, port, proxy, TLS, and firewall behavior without broadly opening access.

title: Correct only the confirmed identity or credential issue
summary: Rotate or replace secrets only after the authentication failure and affected identity are confirmed.
prerequisites: Failure proves authentication or trust issue
rollback: Restore the previous known-good agent configuration if the replacement cannot connect; revoke exposed credentials.
verification: Agent connects with intended identity and permissions.

title: Align Java and Remoting compatibility
summary: Use Jenkins-supported runtime versions and preserve the previous working runtime for rollback.
rollback: Restore the previous working runtime and agent package.
verification: Remoting handshake succeeds and agent stays connected.

title: Repair the confirmed local service failure
summary: Fix the service-specific cause rather than repeatedly restarting it.
prerequisites: User, paths, Java and disk checked
rollback: Revert the configuration or unit change and restore the last known-good service definition.
verification: Process remains stable and Jenkins reports the agent online.

title: Continue with Kubernetes scheduling evidence
summary: A Pending ephemeral agent must be diagnosed from Pod events and scheduling constraints.

title: Continue with container termination evidence
summary: Inspect current/previous logs, termination state, and workload configuration before recreating the agent.

title: Verify stable agent availability
summary: Confirm both connection and actual executor behavior.
verification: A representative safe job can run

title: Escalate with launch method and connection evidence
summary: Preserve the agent log, controller version, launch method, runtime version, and network symptoms without sharing secrets.

title: Diagnosis complete
summary: The reviewed recovery checks passed. Record the cause and prevention step before closing the incident.
prevention: Document the confirmed cause and exact recovery.
Add monitoring or a regression check where practical.
